feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
entry.summary: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

entry.title: True or false: Trump's name is now on the Kennedy Center. The quiz has the answer
entry.summary: The world made it to another Friday without an AI apocalypse, so here's the quiz! See you next week … maybe.

entry.title: How Google is drafting AI chatbot laws around the country
entry.summary: As states push to regulate chatbots, tech companies are trying to write safety rules in ways that exempt some of their key products.

entry.title: Army medics being trained to treat wounded military dogs despite supply challenges
entry.summary: The nature of modern warfare doesn't just mean challenges for treating human casualties. The Army is also training medics to better treat wounded military dogs on the frontlines.

entry.title: Couple shares how chance encounter brought them together after meeting online
entry.summary: A couple, now married, tell the story of how they met online and then crossed paths in an unexpected place.

entry.title: Poland's prime minister warns of Russian 'accidental' attacks on Ukraine's allies
entry.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that these potential strikes "intend to paralyze NATO" in an attempt to demonstrate that Article 5 "exists only in theory."

entry.title: It's illegal for armed federal officers to be at polls. Lawsuits seek to ensure that
entry.summary: The latest lawsuit, first reported by NPR, argues the Trump administration's repeated suggestions that federal officers could be at polling sites is a form of illegal voter intimidation.

entry.title: The driver who slammed into an LA bus before helicopter crash is charged with murder
entry.summary: An SUV driver was under the influence of drugs when she swerved into the wrong lane, blew a red light and slammed into a Los Angeles city bus, killing two riders, prosecutors said as they charged her with murder.

entry.title: Trump withdraws Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, as his nominee to lead ICE
entry.summary: The White House says it is withdrawing its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to lead ICE, ensuring that an agency at the forefront of President Trump's domestic agenda will remain without a Senate-confirmed leader for at least a while longer.

entry.title: ICE agent appears in Minnesota court to face charges in the shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant
entry.summary: Christian Castro, a federal immigration officer, made his first court appearance in Minnesota since he was booked Wednesday into a local jail. Castro faces multiple state and federal charges in connection with a shooting during the immigration surge in Minnesota.
